title: Making recombinant DNA
caption: The gene is isolated and inserted into a vector cut with the same enzyme, ligase joins them, host cells are transformed, and the few cells that took up the plasmid are picked out by a marker gene such as antibiotic resistance. Eukaryotic genes are usually made as cDNA, because bacteria cannot remove introns.
alt: Five boxes in order: isolate the gene, insert it into a vector, join with ligase, transform host cells, and select the transformed cells.
description: Isolate the gene: cut with a restriction enzyme, or make cDNA from mRNA.
Insert it into a vector: a plasmid cut with the same enzyme.
Join with DNA ligase: the sticky ends are sealed.
Transform host cells: a few cells take up the recombinant plasmid.
Select the transformed cells: marker gene: only they grow on the antibiotic.
